units.title: Greetings & Everyday Phrases
units.description: First words in French — Core greetings and polite phrases.

questions.prompt: How do you say "hello (informal)" in French? ___
questions.explanation: "Salut" is the casual hello you use with friends and family; "Bonjour" is the polite one.
questions.example: Salut, Paul ! Tu vas bien ?

questions.prompt: How do you say "hello (formal)" in French?
questions.explanation: "Bonjour" is the polite hello you use with strangers, in shops or at work; "Salut" is only for friends.
questions.example: Bonjour, madame, je voudrais un café.

questions.prompt: How do you say "good evening" in French? ___
questions.explanation: "Bonsoir" is the greeting for the evening. "Bonjour" is used during the day.
questions.example: Bonsoir, tout le monde !

questions.prompt: How do you say "goodbye" in French?
questions.explanation: "Au revoir" is the standard way to say goodbye in any situation; "Bonjour" is hello, not goodbye.
questions.example: Au revoir, et bonne journée !

questions.prompt: How do you say "see you soon" in French? ___
questions.explanation: "À bientôt" means "see you soon": "bientôt" means "soon", and you say it when you expect to meet again before long.
questions.example: À bientôt, j'espère !

questions.audioText: Bonjour, madame, je m'appelle Paul.
questions.explanation: "Bonjour, madame, je m'appelle Paul." is a polite greeting followed by an introduction: "je m'appelle" means "my name is".
"Bonsoir, à bientôt et merci." strings together three useful phrases: "bonsoir" is the evening hello, "à bientôt" means see you soon, and "merci" means thank you.

questions.prompt: Greet a stranger politely and thank them in one short sentence.
acceptableAnswers: Bonjour, merci beaucoup.
Bonjour, merci.
Bonjour, merci bien.
Bonjour, je vous remercie.
Bonjour, merci infiniment.
Bonjour, je vous remercie beaucoup.
Bonjour, merci mille fois.
questions.explanation: "Bonjour, merci beaucoup." combines the polite hello "Bonjour" with "merci beaucoup", meaning "thank you very much".

questions.prompt: How do you say "please" in French?
questions.explanation: "S'il vous plaît" is the polite way to say please; with a friend you say "s'il te plaît".
questions.example: S'il vous plaît, un thé pour moi.

questions.prompt: How do you say "thank you" in French? ___
questions.explanation: "Merci" is the standard way to say "thank you" in French, and it works with anyone.
questions.example: Merci beaucoup pour votre aide.

questions.prompt: How do you say "you're welcome" in French?
questions.explanation: "De rien" literally means "it's nothing" and is the everyday reply when someone says "merci".
questions.example: De rien, c'est normal.

questions.prompt: How do you say "excuse me" in French? ___
questions.explanation: "Excusez-moi" is the polite "excuse me" for getting a stranger's attention. It uses the vous form.
questions.example: Excusez-moi, où est la gare ?

questions.prompt: How do you say "sorry" in French?
questions.explanation: "Désolé" means "sorry" and is used to apologise. A woman writes it "Désolée".
questions.example: Désolé, je suis en retard.

questions.audioText: Excusez-moi, je suis désolé.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "Excusez-moi, je suis désolé." The last word, "désolé", means sorry, and it sounds clearly different from "fatigué", "content" and "malade".

questions.prompt: You are talking to a stranger on the street. Politely ask them (use vous) to speak slowly.
acceptableAnswers: Parlez lentement, s'il vous plaît.
S'il vous plaît, parlez lentement.
Pouvez-vous parler lentement, s'il vous plaît ?
Pouvez-vous parler lentement ?
Pourriez-vous parler lentement, s'il vous plaît ?
Parlez plus lentement, s'il vous plaît.
Parlez doucement, s'il vous plaît.
Pourriez-vous parler plus lentement, s'il vous plaît ?
Pouvez-vous parler plus lentement, s'il vous plaît ?
questions.explanation: "Parlez lentement, s'il vous plaît." uses "parlez", the vous command form of parler, with "lentement" (slowly); "s'il vous plaît" keeps the request polite for a stranger.

questions.prompt: How do you say "yes" in French?
questions.explanation: "Oui" is the French word for "yes". The other options are greetings or welcomes, not answers to a question.
questions.example: Oui, je veux bien un café.

questions.prompt: How do you say "no" in French? ___
questions.explanation: "Non" is the French word for "no", the opposite of "oui".
questions.example: Non, merci, je n'ai pas faim.

questions.prompt: How do you say "how are you?" in French?
questions.explanation: "Comment allez-vous ?" is the polite way to ask how someone is; "Comment vous appelez-vous ?" asks their name instead.
questions.example: Bonjour madame, comment allez-vous ?

questions.prompt: How do you say "I'm fine, thanks" in French? ___
questions.explanation: "Je vais bien, merci" literally means "I am going well, thanks". French uses the verb aller (to go) to say how you are.
questions.example: Je vais bien, merci, et vous ?

questions.prompt: How do you say "what is your name?" in French?
questions.explanation: "Comment vous appelez-vous ?" is the polite way to ask someone's name (literally "how do you call yourself?"); "Je m'appelle..." is the reply.
questions.example: Pardon monsieur, comment vous appelez-vous ?

questions.audioText: Je m'appelle Marie, enchantée.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "Je m'appelle Marie, enchantée.", which means "My name is Marie, nice to meet you." The other choices change one word to something that sounds clearly different.
"Parlez-vous anglais, s'il vous plaît ?" is a polite way to ask a stranger whether they speak English; vous is used with people you don't know.

questions.prompt: Politely ask someone to excuse you, for example to get past them.
acceptableAnswers: Excusez-moi
Excusez-moi, s'il vous plaît
Pardon
Pardon, s'il vous plaît
Excusez-moi, madame
Excusez-moi, monsieur
Pardon, madame
Pardon, monsieur
Excusez-moi, pardon
questions.explanation: "Excusez-moi" is the polite vous form you say to a stranger when you need to get past them; "Pardon" works too.

questions.prompt: How do you say "my name is..." in French? ___
questions.explanation: "Je m'appelle..." means "my name is..." (literally "I call myself"); you follow it with your name.
questions.example: Je m'appelle Marie et j'habite à Lyon.

questions.prompt: How do you say "nice to meet you" in French?
questions.explanation: "Enchanté" is what you say when you meet someone for the first time; a woman writes "Enchantée", which sounds the same.
questions.example: Enchanté, je suis Paul.

questions.prompt: How do you say "good night" in French? ___
questions.explanation: "Bonne nuit" is said at bedtime or late at night when parting; "Au revoir" is just a general goodbye.
questions.example: Bonne nuit, les enfants, à demain !

questions.prompt: How do you say "see you tomorrow" in French?
questions.explanation: "À demain" means "see you tomorrow" because "demain" means "tomorrow".
questions.example: À demain, nous avons cours à huit heures.

questions.prompt: How do you say "welcome" in French? ___
questions.explanation: "Bienvenue" is what you say to greet someone arriving, like "welcome" in English.
questions.example: Bienvenue chez nous, entrez !

questions.audioText: Bonsoir, je m'appelle Marie.
questions.explanation: The sentence "Bonsoir, je m'appelle Marie." greets someone in the evening with "Bonsoir" and then gives a name with "je m'appelle".

questions.prompt: Say politely that you are sorry. One word.
acceptableAnswers: Désolé.
Désolée.
Pardon.
Je suis désolé.
Je suis désolée.
Excusez-moi.
questions.explanation: "Désolé." is the simple way to say you are sorry; a woman writes "Désolée", which sounds the same.

questions.prompt: How do you say "of course" in French? ___
questions.explanation: "Bien sûr" means "of course"; you use it to say yes or to agree warmly.
questions.example: Tu viens ? Bien sûr !

questions.prompt: How do you say "I don't understand" in French?
questions.explanation: "Je ne comprends pas" is the negative of "je comprends" (I understand): French wraps the verb in ne ... pas to say "not".
questions.example: Je ne comprends pas cette question.

questions.prompt: How do you say "can you repeat, please?" in French? ___
bank: Parlez plus lentement, s'il vous plaît
questions.explanation: "Pouvez-vous répéter, s'il vous plaît ?" politely asks someone to say something again: "répéter" means "to repeat" and "pouvez-vous" means "can you".
questions.example: Pouvez-vous répéter, s'il vous plaît ?

questions.prompt: How do you say "do you speak English?" in French?
questions.explanation: "Parlez-vous anglais ?" is a polite question made by putting the verb before "vous"; "anglais" means "English".
questions.example: Parlez-vous anglais ? Je suis perdu.

questions.prompt: How do you say "good luck" in French? ___
questions.explanation: "Bonne chance" means "good luck"; "chance" is feminine, so the adjective is "bonne", not "bon".
questions.example: Bonne chance pour ton examen !

questions.audioText: Je ne comprends pas, désolé.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "Je ne comprends pas, désolé.", meaning "I don't understand, sorry." The other choices change one clearly audible word.
"Je ne comprends pas, excusez-moi" means "I don't understand, excuse me", a polite phrase for when you are lost in a conversation.

questions.prompt: Politely ask someone if they speak French.
acceptableAnswers: Parlez-vous français ?
Est-ce que vous parlez français ?
Vous parlez français ?
Parlez-vous le français ?
Est-ce que vous parlez le français ?
Vous parlez le français ?
Pardon, parlez-vous français ?
Pardon, vous parlez français ?
Excusez-moi, parlez-vous français ?
questions.explanation: "Parlez-vous français ?" is the polite question for "Do you speak French?", with the verb placed before "vous" and "français" meaning "French".

units.title: Numbers 1–100
units.description: Counting in French — Cardinal numbers from one to a hundred.

questions.explanation: "un" is the French number 1; it is also the word for "a" before a masculine noun, as in un café.
questions.example: Il y a un chat dans le jardin.

questions.explanation: "deux" is the French word for 2; the final x is silent when the word stands alone.
questions.example: Elle a deux frères.

questions.explanation: "trois" is the French word for 3; the final s is silent, so it sounds like "trwah".
questions.example: J'ai trois amis ici.

questions.explanation: "quatre" is the French word for 4; it starts with qu-, which sounds like a k.
questions.example: Il a quatre chats.

questions.explanation: "cinq" is the French word for 5; note the unusual -nq spelling at the end.
questions.example: J'ai cinq euros.

questions.audioText: J'ai trois frères et deux sœurs.
choices: J'ai trois frères et dix sœurs.
J'ai trois frères et deux sœurs.
J'ai six frères et deux sœurs.
J'ai trois frères et huit sœurs.
questions.answer: J'ai trois frères et deux sœurs.
questions.explanation: "J'ai trois frères et deux sœurs." means 'I have three brothers and two sisters'; the numbers trois and deux are the words to listen for.

questions.prompt: Say that you have five euros.
acceptableAnswers: J'ai cinq euros.
Moi, j'ai cinq euros.
J'ai 5 euros.
Moi, j'ai 5 euros.
J'ai cinq euros sur moi.
questions.explanation: "J'ai cinq euros." uses j'ai ('I have') followed by the number cinq and the noun euros.
"six" is the French word for 6; it looks like the English word, but on its own it is pronounced "seess", with a clear s sound at the end.
questions.example: Il est six heures.

questions.explanation: "sept" is the French word for 7; the p is silent, so it sounds like "set".
questions.example: Nous sommes sept à table.

questions.explanation: "huit" is the French word for 8; the h is silent and it sounds like "weet".
questions.example: Ma sœur a huit ans.

questions.explanation: "neuf" means nine (9); don't mix it up with "cinq" (5) or "treize" (13).
questions.example: Il y a neuf élèves.

questions.explanation: "dix" means ten (10); it is the base for 17, 18 and 19 ("dix-sept", "dix-huit", "dix-neuf").
questions.example: Il est dix heures.

questions.audioText: J'ai huit ans.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "J'ai huit ans.", meaning I am eight years old; huit sounds like "weet" and is clearly different from dix, neuf and sept.
"Il y a dix euros" means there are ten euros; before the vowel of euros, the x of dix links as a z sound, so you say "di-zeuro".

questions.prompt: Say that you have nine euros.
acceptableAnswers: J'ai neuf euros.
Moi, j'ai neuf euros.
J'ai 9 euros.
Moi, j'ai 9 euros.
questions.explanation: "J'ai neuf euros." uses j'ai (I have) followed by neuf, the word for nine.
"onze" means eleven (11); it is the first of the special words for 11 to 16, so it is not built from "dix".
questions.example: J'ai onze ans.

questions.explanation: "douze" means twelve (12); it comes right after "onze" (11).
questions.example: Nous avons douze œufs.

questions.explanation: "treize" means thirteen (13); like the other numbers from 11 to 16, it ends in -ze.
questions.example: Elle a treize ans.

questions.explanation: "quatorze" means fourteen (14); it comes from "quatre" (4), like fourteen comes from four.
questions.example: Il y a quatorze personnes ici.

questions.explanation: "quinze" means fifteen (15); "quatorze" is 14, so don't mix them up.
questions.example: Mon frère a quinze ans.

questions.audioText: J'ai quinze euros.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "J'ai quinze euros.", which means I have fifteen euros; quinze is 15, so don't mix it up with treize, douze or onze.

questions.prompt: Say that you have fourteen euros.
acceptableAnswers: J'ai quatorze euros.
Moi, j'ai quatorze euros.
J'ai 14 euros.
Moi, j'ai 14 euros.
questions.explanation: "J'ai quatorze euros." uses j'ai (I have) with quatorze, the French word for fourteen (14).
"seize" means sixteen (16); it is the last special word before French counts "dix-sept" (ten-seven).
questions.example: Ma cousine a seize ans.

questions.explanation: "dix-sept" means seventeen: ten ("dix") plus seven ("sept"), joined with a hyphen.
questions.example: Il a dix-sept ans.

questions.explanation: "dix-huit" means eighteen: ten ("dix") plus eight ("huit"), joined with a hyphen.
questions.example: Elle a dix-huit ans.

questions.explanation: "dix-neuf" is built as dix (ten) + neuf (nine), joined with a hyphen, just like "dix-huit" (eighteen).
questions.example: Mon voisin a dix-neuf ans.

questions.explanation: "vingt" means twenty. Its final -gt is silent, so it sounds like "vin".
questions.example: Ma tante a vingt ans.

questions.audioText: J'ai dix-sept ans.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "J'ai dix-sept ans." (I am seventeen years old); dix-sept sounds different from dix-huit, seize and vingt.
"J'ai dix-neuf euros" means I have nineteen euros; dix-neuf is ten plus nine, joined with a hyphen.

questions.prompt: Say the number that comes right after sixteen.
acceptableAnswers: dix-sept
C'est dix-sept.
Le nombre est dix-sept.
C'est le dix-sept.
C'est 17.
Après seize, c'est dix-sept.
questions.explanation: The number after sixteen is seventeen, written "dix-sept": ten ("dix") plus seven ("sept"), joined with a hyphen.
"vingt et un" means twenty-one; 21, 31, 41 and so on use "et" (and), unlike "vingt-deux" (22).
questions.example: Ma mère a vingt et un ans.

questions.explanation: "trente" means thirty (30); it is the tens word that comes after "vingt" (20).
questions.example: Il y a trente élèves dans la classe.

questions.explanation: "quarante" means forty; don't mix it up with "quatre" (four) or "cent" (one hundred).
questions.example: Mon père a quarante ans.

questions.explanation: "cinquante" means fifty; it starts like "cinq" (five), just as fifty starts like five.
questions.example: Ma grand-mère a cinquante ans.

questions.prompt: The French word for "one hundred" is…
questions.explanation: "cent" means one hundred; French just says "cent", not "un cent".
questions.example: Il y a cent personnes ici.

questions.audioText: J'ai quarante ans.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "J'ai quarante ans.", meaning 'I am forty years old'; French uses avoir (to have) for age, and "quarante" is forty.

questions.prompt: Say that you have fifty euros.
acceptableAnswers: J'ai cinquante euros.
Moi, j'ai cinquante euros.
J'ai 50 euros.
Moi, j'ai 50 euros.
questions.explanation: "J'ai cinquante euros." uses "j'ai" (I have) followed by "cinquante" (fifty) and the noun "euros".

units.title: Family & People
units.description: Talking about people you know — Family members and everyday words for people.

questions.explanation: "la mère" means mother; "la" shows it is a feminine noun, unlike "le fils" (son) or "le voisin" (neighbour).
questions.example: La mère de Julie travaille ici.

questions.explanation: "le père" means father; its partner word is "la mère" (mother).
questions.example: Le père de Paul est médecin.

questions.explanation: "la sœur" means sister. It is feminine, so it takes "la", and it is spelled with the joined letters œ.
questions.example: La sœur de Marc a dix ans.

questions.explanation: "le frère" means brother, a male sibling; don't confuse it with "la sœur" (sister) or "le cousin" (cousin).
questions.example: Le frère de Marc aime le foot.

questions.explanation: "le fils" means son; the final s is pronounced ("feess"). "l'enfant" means any child, not specifically a son.
questions.example: Le fils de Paul s'appelle Hugo.

questions.audioText: Mon père est ici.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "Mon père est ici.", meaning my father is here. The wrong choices change one word you can hear: mère, frère or là-bas.

questions.answer: Voici ma sœur et mon frère
questions.explanation: "Voici ma sœur et mon frère" means here are my sister and my brother. Use "ma" with the feminine sœur and "mon" with the masculine frère.

questions.prompt: Say that your mother has a son.
acceptableAnswers: Ma mère a un fils.
Ma mère a un garçon.
Ma mère a un enfant, un fils.
Ma maman a un fils.
Ma mère a un petit garçon.
questions.explanation: "Ma mère a un fils." uses "a" (has) from avoir, "ma" for the feminine mère, and "un fils" for a son.
"la fille" means daughter (it also means girl). "le fils" is the son and "la sœur" is the sister.
questions.example: La fille de Léa est très gentille.

questions.explanation: "la grand-mère" means grandmother: grand + mère (mother), joined with a hyphen.
questions.example: La grand-mère de Léa fait des gâteaux.

questions.explanation: "le grand-père" means grandfather: grand + père (father). "la grand-mère" is the grandmother.
questions.example: Le grand-père de Tom habite à Nice.

questions.explanation: "la tante" means aunt, the sister of your mother or father.
questions.example: La tante de Marc vit à Paris.

questions.explanation: "l'oncle" means uncle. The word is masculine (un oncle), and le becomes l' before the vowel.
questions.example: L'oncle de Paul est pilote.

questions.audioText: Ma tante est la sœur de mon père.
choices: Ma tante est la sœur de mon frère.
Ma tante est la sœur de mon père.
Ma tante est la femme de mon père.
Ma fille est la sœur de mon père.
questions.answer: Ma tante est la sœur de mon père.
questions.explanation: The sentence is "Ma tante est la sœur de mon père." and it means 'My aunt is my father's sister.' The other choices change one word: fille, femme or frère.

questions.prompt: Say that your grandmother is a friend of your aunt.
acceptableAnswers: Ma grand-mère est une amie de ma tante.
Ma grand-mère est l'amie de ma tante.
Ma grand-mère est amie avec ma tante.
Ma mamie est une amie de ma tante.
questions.explanation: "Ma grand-mère est une amie de ma tante." uses ma before the feminine words grand-mère and tante, and une amie because the friend is a woman. De links the friend to the person she is a friend of.
"le cousin" is a male cousin; the masculine form ends in -in, pronounced nasally.
questions.example: Le cousin de Luc joue au foot.

questions.explanation: "la cousine" is a female cousin: add -e to le cousin and pronounce the n. "le cousin" is the male form.
questions.example: La cousine de Sara a six ans.

questions.explanation: "le mari" means husband. For wife, French usually says la femme.
questions.example: Le mari de Claire est cuisinier.

questions.explanation: "l'épouse" means wife; in everyday speech French more often says "ma femme" (my wife).
questions.example: L'épouse de Marc est professeur.

questions.explanation: "l'ami" is a male friend; a female friend is "l'amie", with an extra -e.
questions.example: L'ami de Paul s'appelle Hugo.

questions.audioText: Mon cousin est très gentil.
questions.explanation: The sentence is "Mon cousin est très gentil." and it means 'My cousin is very nice.' Voisin rhymes with cousin, so listen for the first sound: cousin starts with a k sound.
"Mon ami est mon voisin." means "My friend is my neighbor." Use mon before ami and voisin, since both are masculine words for a male friend and a male neighbor.

questions.prompt: Say that your husband is a friend of your cousin (a male cousin).
acceptableAnswers: Mon mari est l'ami de mon cousin.
Mon mari est un ami de mon cousin.
Mon époux est l'ami de mon cousin.
Mon époux est un ami de mon cousin.
Mon mari est ami avec mon cousin.
Mon mari est copain avec mon cousin.
questions.explanation: "Mon mari est l'ami de mon cousin." uses mari for husband and ami for a male friend, joined by de to show whose friend he is.
"l'amie" is a female friend; the extra -e marks the feminine (a male friend is "l'ami").
questions.example: L'amie de Léa est très drôle.

questions.explanation: "l'homme" means man; the h is silent, so le becomes l'.
questions.example: L'homme porte un chapeau noir.

questions.explanation: "la femme" means woman (and also wife); it is pronounced "fam".
questions.example: La femme lit un livre.

questions.explanation: "l'enfant" means child, a boy or a girl; le or la becomes l' before the vowel.
questions.example: L'enfant joue dans le jardin.

questions.explanation: "le bébé" means "baby". The noun is masculine, so it takes "le" even when the baby is a girl.
questions.example: Le bébé dort dans la chambre.

questions.audioText: Mon ami habite avec sa mère.
choices: Mon ami habite avec sa tante.
Mon ami habite avec son frère.
Mon ami habite avec sa mère.
Mon ami habite avec son père.
questions.answer: Mon ami habite avec sa mère.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "Mon ami habite avec sa mère.", meaning my friend lives with his mother; "mère" (mother) sounds clearly different from père, tante and frère.

questions.prompt: Say that your friend (a woman) has a baby.
acceptableAnswers: Mon amie a un bébé.
Mon amie a un petit bébé.
Mon amie a un enfant.
questions.explanation: "Mon amie a un bébé." uses "amie" for a female friend, "a" for has, and "bébé", which is masculine and takes "un".
"le garçon" means "boy". Its counterpart for a girl is "la fille".
questions.example: Le garçon mange une pomme.

questions.explanation: "le voisin" means "neighbour", the person who lives next door. A female neighbour is "la voisine".
questions.example: Le voisin est très gentil.

questions.explanation: "le collègue" means "colleague", someone you work with. Note the accent on the first e, and that a woman is "la collègue".
questions.example: Le collègue de Paul arrive à huit heures.

questions.explanation: "le professeur" means "teacher", especially in secondary school. In everyday speech people often shorten it to "le prof".
questions.example: Le professeur parle doucement.

questions.explanation: "l'étudiant" means a (male) student; a female student is "l'étudiante".
questions.example: L'étudiant lit dans la bibliothèque.

questions.audioText: Le voisin est mon ami.
questions.explanation: The sentence "Le voisin est mon ami." means "The neighbour is my friend." The wrong choices change one clearly different word: garçon, oncle or collègue.
"Mon voisin est étudiant" means 'My neighbor is a student.' French leaves out the article after être when you give someone's job or status, so you say "est étudiant", not "est un étudiant".

questions.prompt: Say that your colleague is a student.
acceptableAnswers: Mon collègue est étudiant.
Mon collègue est un étudiant.
Ma collègue est étudiante.
Ma collègue est une étudiante.
questions.explanation: "Mon collègue est étudiant." says your colleague is a student. After être, French usually drops the article before a profession or status like étudiant.

units.title: Colours & Clothes
units.description: Describing what people wear — Common colours and clothing items.

questions.explanation: "rouge" means "red". It already ends in -e, so it stays the same for masculine and feminine nouns.
questions.example: Le feu est rouge.

questions.explanation: "bleu" means blue; "gris", "vert" and "violet" mean grey, green and purple.
questions.example: Le ciel est bleu aujourd'hui.

questions.explanation: "vert" means green; "noir", "rouge" and "rose" mean black, red and pink.
questions.example: L'herbe est verte.

questions.explanation: "jaune" means yellow; "rouge", "noir" and "marron" mean red, black and brown.
questions.example: Le citron est jaune.

questions.explanation: "noir" means black; "violet" is purple, "bleu" is blue and "gris" is grey.
questions.example: Mon chat est noir.

questions.audioText: Elle porte une robe rouge.
questions.explanation: The sentence heard is "Elle porte une robe rouge.", meaning she is wearing a red dress. The other choices change only the colour.

questions.prompt: Say that the car is green.
acceptableAnswers: La voiture est verte.
La voiture est de couleur verte.
C'est une voiture verte.

"blanc" means white; "noir" is black, "bleu" is blue and "rose" is pink.

questions.explanation: "gris" means grey; "marron" is brown, "jaune" is yellow and "rouge" is red.

questions.explanation: "marron" means brown, and it never changes its ending (des chaussures marron); "gris" is grey, "vert" is green and "blanc" is white.

questions.explanation: "rose" means pink; "bleu" is blue, "noir" is black and "violet" is purple.
questions.example: Elle porte une robe rose.

questions.explanation: "violet" means purple; "rouge" is red, "jaune" is yellow and "marron" is brown.
questions.example: Mon sac est violet.

questions.audioText: Elle porte une robe rose.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "Elle porte une robe rose." meaning she is wearing a pink dress; the other choices name different colours.
"Il porte un pull gris" means 'He is wearing a grey sweater', using the colour gris after the clothing word.

questions.prompt: Say that he is wearing a white shirt.
acceptableAnswers: Il porte une chemise blanche.
Il a une chemise blanche.
Il est en chemise blanche.
Il a une chemise blanche sur lui.
questions.explanation: "Il porte une chemise blanche." uses porter for wearing, and blanche is feminine to agree with chemise.
"la chemise" means a shirt; "la robe" is a dress, "les gants" are gloves and "la veste" is a jacket.

questions.explanation: "le pantalon" means trousers, and it is singular in French although "trousers" is plural in English; "la jupe" is a skirt, "le pull" a sweater and "la chemise" a shirt.

questions.explanation: "la robe" means a dress; "les bottes" are boots, "le manteau" is a coat and "la jupe" is a skirt.

questions.explanation: "la jupe" means a skirt; "les bottes" are boots, "le manteau" is a coat and "les chaussettes" are socks.

questions.audioText: Elle porte une jupe rouge.
questions.explanation: The sentence "Elle porte une jupe rouge." means she is wearing a red skirt; the other choices change the clothing or the colour.

questions.prompt: Say that he is wearing a blue shirt.
acceptableAnswers: Il porte une chemise bleue.
Il a une chemise bleue.
Il est vêtu d'une chemise bleue.
Il est en chemise bleue.
Il porte une chemise de couleur bleue.
questions.explanation: "Il porte une chemise bleue." uses porter for wearing, and the adjective bleue agrees with the feminine noun la chemise.
"les chaussures" means shoes; "la veste" is a jacket, "les gants" are gloves and "le pantalon" is trousers.
questions.example: Les chaussures sont neuves.

questions.explanation: A jacket is "la veste"; it is feminine, so it takes "la". Don't confuse it with "le manteau", which is a longer, warmer coat.

questions.explanation: A coat is "le manteau"; it is masculine, so it takes "le". A lighter jacket would be "la veste".
questions.example: Le manteau est dans l'entrée.

questions.explanation: A hat is "le chapeau"; it is masculine, and its plural adds -x: "les chapeaux".
questions.example: Le chapeau de Paul est noir.

questions.explanation: A scarf is "l'écharpe"; the word is feminine, but "la" shortens to "l'" before the vowel "é".
questions.example: L'écharpe de Léa est rouge.

questions.audioText: Elle porte une robe rouge aujourd'hui.
choices: Elle porte une robe rouge aujourd'hui.
Elle porte une robe rouge hier.
Elle porte une jupe rouge aujourd'hui.
Elle porte une robe verte aujourd'hui.
questions.answer: Elle porte une robe rouge aujourd'hui.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "Elle porte une robe rouge aujourd'hui." meaning she is wearing a red dress today; the other choices change the colour, the clothing or the day.
"Il porte un manteau noir" means he is wearing a black coat; "manteau" is masculine, so it takes "un" and the colour stays in the masculine form.

questions.prompt: Say that the woman is wearing a blue skirt.
acceptableAnswers: La femme porte une jupe bleue.
Elle porte une jupe bleue.
La dame porte une jupe bleue.
Elle a une jupe bleue.
La femme a une jupe bleue.
La femme est vêtue d'une jupe bleue.
Elle est vêtue d'une jupe bleue.
La femme est en jupe bleue.
Elle est en jupe bleue.
questions.explanation: "La femme porte une jupe bleue." uses "porte" for wearing, and "bleue" takes an -e because "jupe" is feminine.
Socks are "les chaussettes"; don't confuse them with "les chaussures", which are shoes.
questions.example: Les chaussettes sont dans le tiroir.

questions.explanation: A sweater is "le pull", short for "le pull-over"; it is masculine, so it takes "le".
questions.example: Le pull est trop petit.

questions.explanation: A belt is "la ceinture"; it is feminine, so it takes "la".
questions.example: La ceinture de Paul est noire.

questions.explanation: Gloves are "les gants"; they come in pairs, so the word is plural with "les" (one glove is "un gant").
questions.example: Les gants sont dans mon sac.

questions.explanation: Boots are "les bottes"; the word is plural, so it takes "les" (one boot is "une botte").
questions.example: Les bottes sont à la porte.

questions.audioText: Elle porte une robe bleue.
questions.explanation: The sentence is "Elle porte une robe bleue." and means 'She is wearing a blue dress.'; "robe" (dress) and "bleue" (blue) are the words to listen for.

questions.prompt: Say that he is wearing a blue sweater.
acceptableAnswers: Il porte un pull bleu.
Il a un pull bleu.
Il est vêtu d'un pull bleu.
Il est en pull bleu.
Il porte un chandail bleu.
Il porte un tricot bleu.
questions.explanation: "Il porte un pull bleu." uses porter for wearing; the adjective bleu comes after the masculine noun pull.

units.title: Days, Months & Seasons
units.description: Talking about time and calendar — Days of the week, months, and seasons.

lessons.title: Days, Months & Seasons 1
lessons.subtitle: Talking about time and the calendar

questions.explanation: "lundi" means "Monday", the first day of the French week. Days of the week take no capital letter in French.
questions.example: Lundi, je travaille à la maison.

questions.explanation: "mardi" means "Tuesday", the day after "lundi". It is written with a small letter in French.
questions.example: Mardi, nous avons un examen.

questions.explanation: "mercredi" means "Wednesday", the middle of the week. It is written with a small letter in French.
questions.example: Mercredi, les enfants ne vont pas à l'école.

questions.explanation: "jeudi" means "Thursday", the day after "mercredi". It is written with a small letter in French.
questions.example: Jeudi soir, je vais au cinéma.

questions.explanation: Friday is "vendredi", the day after "jeudi" (Thursday). French day names are written in lowercase.
questions.example: Vendredi, nous mangeons au restaurant.

questions.audioText: Aujourd'hui, c'est lundi.
questions.explanation: The sentence "Aujourd'hui, c'est lundi." means "Today is Monday." The other choices name different days: mardi, jeudi and samedi.
"Aujourd'hui, c'est vendredi" means "Today is Friday." French uses "c'est" plus the day name to say which day it is, and the day name stays in lowercase.

acceptableAnswers: Aujourd'hui, c'est mercredi.
Aujourd'hui, nous sommes mercredi.
C'est mercredi aujourd'hui.
Nous sommes mercredi aujourd'hui.
On est mercredi aujourd'hui.
Aujourd'hui, on est mercredi.
Nous sommes mercredi.
questions.explanation: "Aujourd'hui, c'est mercredi." is the usual way to say that today is Wednesday. In French the day name takes no capital letter.

lessons.title: Days, Months & Seasons 2
lessons.subtitle: Talking about time and the calendar

questions.explanation: Saturday is "samedi"; don't confuse it with "dimanche", which is Sunday, the day after.
questions.example: Samedi, nous allons au marché.

questions.explanation: Sunday is "dimanche"; it is the only day of the week that does not end in -di.
questions.example: Dimanche, on dort tard.

questions.explanation: "janvier" means January. Unlike in English, French month names start with a lowercase letter.
questions.example: Il fait très froid en janvier.

questions.explanation: "février" means February. Note the accent on the first e (é) and the lowercase f.
questions.example: Mon anniversaire est en février.

questions.explanation: "mars" means March. It looks like the English word, but it is not capitalised and the final s is pronounced.
questions.example: Le printemps commence en mars.

questions.audioText: Aujourd'hui, c'est lundi et il pleut.
choices: Aujourd'hui, c'est lundi et il pleut.
Aujourd'hui, c'est lundi et il vente.
Aujourd'hui, c'est lundi et il neige.
Aujourd'hui, c'est jeudi et il pleut.
questions.answer: Aujourd'hui, c'est lundi et il pleut.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "Aujourd'hui, c'est lundi et il pleut.", meaning today is Monday and it is raining; "lundi" (Monday) and "pleut" (rains) are the key words to listen for.

questions.prompt: Say that your birthday is in March.
acceptableAnswers: Mon anniversaire est en mars.
Mon anniversaire, c'est en mars.
Mon anniversaire est au mois de mars.
Mon anniversaire tombe en mars.
C'est en mars, mon anniversaire.
questions.explanation: "Mon anniversaire est en mars." uses en before a month name to mean in, and the month stays lowercase in French.

lessons.title: Days, Months & Seasons 3
lessons.subtitle: Talking about time and the calendar

questions.explanation: "avril" means April. It is close to the English word, with a v instead of the p, and it is written in lowercase.
questions.example: Nous partons en vacances en avril.

questions.explanation: "mai" means May. It sounds much like the English word and, like all French months, it is written in lowercase.
questions.example: En mai, il y a beaucoup de fleurs.

questions.explanation: "juin" means June. Don't confuse it with "juillet" (July), which is the longer word.
questions.example: L'école finit en juin.

questions.explanation: "juillet" means July. The double l and the -et ending set it apart from "juin" (June).
questions.example: Nous allons à la mer en juillet.

questions.explanation: "août" means August. Remember the circumflex on the u; the word is pronounced like "oo" or "oot".
questions.example: Il fait très chaud en août.

questions.audioText: Mon anniversaire est en juin.
questions.explanation: The sentence "Mon anniversaire est en juin." means 'My birthday is in June.' The months juin, mai, août and avril all sound clearly different.
"Nous sommes en août" means 'It is August' (literally 'We are in August'). Use "en" before a month in French.

questions.prompt: Say that your birthday is in the month of June.
acceptableAnswers: Mon anniversaire est en juin.
C'est en juin, mon anniversaire.
Mon anniversaire, c'est en juin.
Mon anniversaire est au mois de juin.
Mon anniversaire, c'est au mois de juin.
Mon anniversaire tombe en juin.
Mon anniversaire est dans le mois de juin.
questions.explanation: "Mon anniversaire est en juin." uses "en" before a month to mean "in", and the month stays in lowercase.

lessons.title: Days, Months & Seasons 4
lessons.subtitle: Talking about time and the calendar

questions.explanation: "septembre" means September. It is like the English word, but it ends in -bre and is written in lowercase.
questions.example: L'école commence en septembre.

questions.explanation: "octobre" means "October". Like all French months, it is written with a small letter.
questions.example: Il pleut souvent en octobre.

questions.explanation: "novembre" means "November", the month after "octobre". French months are written with a small letter.
questions.example: Il fait déjà froid en novembre.

questions.explanation: December is "décembre". In French, month names take no capital letter, and note the accent on the é.
questions.example: Noël est en décembre.

questions.explanation: Spring is "le printemps". It is the only season that keeps "le", because it starts with a consonant; you say "au printemps" for "in spring".
questions.example: Le printemps est ma saison préférée.

questions.audioText: Mon anniversaire est en décembre.
questions.explanation: The sentence "Mon anniversaire est en décembre." means 'My birthday is in December.' The month is the key word, and each month sounds clearly different.

acceptableAnswers: J'aime le printemps.
J'aime bien le printemps.
Moi, j'aime le printemps.
J'adore le printemps.
Moi, j'aime bien le printemps.
J'aime beaucoup le printemps.
questions.explanation: "J'aime le printemps." uses "j'aime" (I like) followed by "le printemps" (spring). In French you keep "le" when you speak about a season in general.

lessons.title: Days, Months & Seasons 5
lessons.subtitle: Talking about time and the calendar

questions.explanation: Summer is "l'été". "Le" shortens to "l'" before a vowel, and "in summer" is "en été".
questions.example: L'été, nous allons à la plage.

questions.explanation: Autumn is "l'automne". The "m" is silent, so it sounds like "o-tonn", and "in autumn" is "en automne".
questions.example: L'automne, les feuilles tombent.

questions.explanation: Winter is "l'hiver". The h is silent, so "le" shortens to "l'", and "in winter" is "en hiver".
questions.example: L'hiver, il neige dans les Alpes.

questions.explanation: Today is "aujourd'hui". Don't confuse it with "maintenant" (now) or "ce soir" (tonight).
questions.example: Aujourd'hui, il fait beau.

questions.explanation: Tomorrow is "demain". Its opposite is "hier" (yesterday).
questions.example: Demain, je vais chez le médecin.

questions.audioText: Nous sommes en hiver aujourd'hui.
questions.explanation: The sentence "Nous sommes en hiver aujourd'hui." means we are in winter today; the other choices change the season or swap "aujourd'hui" for "demain".
"Demain, c'est lundi" means tomorrow is Monday, using "demain" for tomorrow and a day of the week.

questions.prompt: Say that it is summer now.
acceptableAnswers: C'est l'été maintenant.
Nous sommes en été maintenant.
Maintenant, c'est l'été.
Maintenant, nous sommes en été.

C'est l'été à présent.
Nous sommes en été à présent.
questions.explanation: "C'est l'été maintenant." uses "l'été" for summer and "maintenant" for now; "nous sommes en été" is another natural way to say it.

units.title: Body Parts
units.description: Talking about the human body — Common parts of the body.

questions.explanation: Head is "la tête". It is feminine, so it takes "la", and the ê has a circumflex.

questions.explanation: Hair on your head is "les cheveux". It is plural in French, unlike English; "un cheveu" is a single hair.
questions.example: Elle a les cheveux longs.

questions.explanation: Eye is "l'œil". Its plural is completely different: "les yeux" (eyes).
questions.example: J'ai mal à l'œil droit.

questions.explanation: "les yeux" means eyes. It is the irregular plural of "l'œil" (eye).
questions.example: Il a les yeux bleus.

questions.explanation: "l'oreille" means ear. It is a feminine noun, and le/la becomes l' before a vowel sound.
questions.example: Il a mal à l'oreille.

questions.audioText: J'ai mal à la tête.
questions.explanation: "J'ai mal à la tête." means I have a headache; "la tête" (head) sounds clearly different from "la main" (hand), "la dent" (tooth) and "la bouche" (mouth).

questions.prompt: Say that your hair is long.
acceptableAnswers: Mes cheveux sont longs.
J'ai les cheveux longs.
Mes cheveux sont très longs.
Mes cheveux sont assez longs.
J'ai de longs cheveux.
J'ai les cheveux assez longs.

"le nez" means nose. It is masculine, and the final z is silent.

questions.explanation: "le cou" means "neck". It is masculine, so it takes le; don't confuse it with le coude (elbow).

questions.explanation: "l'épaule" means "shoulder". It is feminine (une épaule), and la becomes l' before the vowel sound é.

questions.audioText: Elle ouvre la bouche.
questions.explanation: "Elle ouvre la bouche." means "She opens her mouth". Listen for the noun at the end: bouche (mouth) sounds clearly different from porte (door), main (hand) or fenêtre (window).
"Ouvre la bouche" means Open your mouth; la bouche is feminine, so it takes la.

questions.prompt: Say that you have a sore neck.

questions.audioText: J'ai mal au bras

acceptableAnswers: J'ai mal à la main.

La main me fait mal.

"le ventre" means "stomach" or "belly", as in « J'ai mal au ventre » (I have a stomach ache). It is masculine, so it takes le.

questions.explanation: "la jambe" means "leg". It is feminine, so it takes la; don't confuse it with le pied (foot).

questions.explanation: Knee is "le genou". It is masculine, and its plural ends in x: "les genoux".

questions.explanation: Foot is "le pied". The d is silent, and "on foot" is "à pied".

questions.explanation: "Skin" is "la peau", a feminine noun. Don't confuse it with "la poitrine", which means chest.

questions.audioText: J'ai mal au ventre aujourd'hui.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "J'ai mal au ventre aujourd'hui." meaning they have a stomach ache today; the other choices name a knee, a foot or an arm.
"J'ai mal à la jambe" means "My leg hurts." La jambe is feminine, so the French uses à la before it.

acceptableAnswers: J'ai mal au pied.

J'ai le pied qui me fait mal.

"Face" is "le visage". It is masculine even though it ends in -e.

questions.explanation: "Heart" is "le cœur", a masculine noun spelled with the joined letters œ.

questions.explanation: "Elbow" is "le coude". "Le bras" is the whole arm, not the joint in the middle.

questions.explanation: "Wrist" is "le poignet", a masculine noun. The final t is silent.

questions.explanation: "Chin" is "le menton". "Le nez" is the nose, just above it.
questions.example: Il a le menton pointu.

questions.audioText: J'ai mal au dos.
questions.explanation: The sentence is "J'ai mal au dos." It means my back hurts; "dos" is the back, which sounds different from "cœur", "cou" and "nez".

acceptableAnswers: J'ai mal au menton.
Mon menton me fait mal.
Le menton me fait mal.
J'ai le menton douloureux.
questions.explanation: "J'ai mal au menton." uses "avoir mal à" plus the body part, and "à + le" becomes "au" before the masculine noun "menton".

units.title: House & Rooms
units.description: Talking about where you live — Rooms and household vocabulary.

questions.explanation: "House" is "la maison", a feminine noun, so you say une maison.
questions.example: La maison de Paul est grande.

questions.explanation: "Apartment" is "l'appartement". The article becomes l' before a vowel. The word is masculine (un appartement) and is spelled with a double p.
questions.example: L'appartement est au troisième étage.

questions.explanation: "la cuisine" means "kitchen", the room where you cook. It is feminine, and the same word also means cooking or cuisine.
questions.example: La cuisine est très propre.

questions.explanation: "la chambre" is the room where you sleep, so it means "bedroom". Don't confuse it with "la salle à manger", the dining room.
questions.example: La chambre de Léa est rose.

questions.explanation: "la salle de bain" literally means "room of bath", the room where you wash, so it is the "bathroom".
questions.example: La salle de bain est petite.

questions.audioText: J'habite dans une petite maison.
questions.explanation: "J'habite dans une petite maison." means "I live in a small house." The key words are "petite" (small) and "maison" (house).

questions.answer: Ma chambre est à côté de la cuisine
questions.explanation: "Ma chambre est à côté de la cuisine" means "My bedroom is next to the kitchen." The phrase "à côté de" tells you where one room is in relation to another.

questions.prompt: Say that you live in an apartment.
acceptableAnswers: J'habite dans un appartement.
J'habite un appartement.
Je vis dans un appartement.
J'habite en appartement.
Je vis en appartement.
J'habite dans un appart.
Je vis dans un appart.
questions.explanation: "J'habite dans un appartement." means "I live in an apartment." The word appartement is masculine, so it takes un.

questions.prompt: The French word for "living room" is…
questions.explanation: "le salon" is the room where you sit, relax and welcome guests, so it means "living room".
questions.example: Le salon est grand et lumineux.

questions.prompt: The French word for "dining room" is… ___
questions.explanation: "la salle à manger" literally means "room for eating" (manger = to eat), so it is the "dining room".
questions.example: La salle à manger est à gauche.

questions.explanation: "le jardin" is the outdoor area with grass, flowers or vegetables next to a house, so it means "garden".
questions.example: Le jardin est plein de fleurs.

questions.explanation: "la porte" is what you open and close to go into a room or a house, so it means "door".
questions.example: La porte est fermée.

questions.explanation: "la fenêtre" is the glass opening in a wall that lets light in, so it means "window".
questions.example: La fenêtre est ouverte.

questions.audioText: Nous avons un grand jardin.
questions.explanation: The sentence is "Nous avons un grand jardin." and means "We have a big garden." The other choices change the noun to a different room or object.

questions.prompt: Say that the living room is next to the kitchen.
acceptableAnswers: Le salon est à côté de la cuisine.
Le salon est près de la cuisine.
Le salon se trouve à côté de la cuisine.
Le salon est situé à côté de la cuisine.
Le salon est juste à côté de la cuisine.
Le salon est voisin de la cuisine.
questions.explanation: "Le salon est à côté de la cuisine." uses "à côté de" to mean "next to"; "près de" (near) is also a natural way to say it.
"le mur" is each vertical side of a room or building, so it means "wall".
questions.example: Le mur est blanc.

questions.explanation: "le sol" is the surface you walk on inside a room, so it means "floor". "le toit" is the roof and "le tapis" is a rug.
questions.example: Le sol est froid.

questions.explanation: "le plafond" is the top surface of a room, above your head, so it means "ceiling".
questions.example: Le plafond est très haut.

questions.explanation: "l'escalier" is the set of steps leading to another floor; French uses the singular where English says "stairs".
questions.example: L'escalier est devant la porte.

questions.explanation: "Roof" is "le toit", a masculine noun. The final t is silent.
questions.example: Le toit est rouge.

questions.audioText: La table est dans la cuisine.
choices: La lampe est dans la cuisine.
La table est dans la cuisine.
La chaise est dans la cuisine.
La table est dans la chambre.
questions.answer: La table est dans la cuisine.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "La table est dans la cuisine.", meaning the table is in the kitchen; the other choices change the object (chaise, lampe) or the room (chambre).

questions.answer: Le mur de la cuisine est blanc.
questions.explanation: In "Le mur de la cuisine est blanc." you describe a wall with a color: "est" links the noun to the adjective, and "blanc" is masculine because "le mur" is masculine.

questions.prompt: Say that your house has a big kitchen.
acceptableAnswers: Ma maison a une grande cuisine.
J'ai une grande cuisine dans ma maison.
Dans ma maison, il y a une grande cuisine.
Ma maison possède une grande cuisine.
Ma maison a une cuisine spacieuse.
Ma maison a une cuisine de grande taille.
Il y a une grande cuisine dans ma maison.
questions.explanation: "Ma maison a une grande cuisine." uses avoir to say what the house has; "grande" goes before the feminine noun "cuisine".
"Garage" is "le garage", a masculine noun. Careful: "la gare" means train station.
questions.example: Le garage est derrière la maison.

questions.explanation: "Table" is "la table", a feminine noun. "Le tableau" looks similar but means a painting or a board.
questions.meaning: furniture with legs for eating at
questions.example: La table est dans la cuisine.

questions.explanation: "Chair" is "la chaise", a feminine noun. Don't mix it up with "la porte", the door.
questions.meaning: seat with a back for one person
questions.example: La chaise est confortable.

questions.explanation: "le lit" means bed, the piece of furniture you sleep in. Lit is masculine, so it takes "le". Don't confuse it with la chambre, the bedroom.
questions.example: Le lit est très grand.

questions.explanation: "le canapé" means sofa (couch). Canapé is masculine, so it takes "le".
questions.example: Le canapé est dans le salon.

questions.audioText: J'habite dans une grande maison.
questions.explanation: The sentence is "J'habite dans une grande maison.", meaning I live in a big house. The other choices change only the final noun, which sounds clearly different.

questions.prompt: Say that you live in a house with a garden.
acceptableAnswers: J'habite dans une maison avec un jardin.
J'habite une maison avec un jardin.
Je vis dans une maison avec un jardin.
J'habite dans une maison avec jardin.
Je vis dans une maison avec jardin.
J'habite une maison avec jardin.
J'habite une maison qui a un jardin.
Je vis dans une maison qui a un jardin.
questions.explanation: "J'habite dans une maison avec un jardin." uses "habiter" to say where you live, and "avec" means 'with'. "Maison" is feminine so it takes "une", while "jardin" is masculine so it takes "un".
"la lampe" means lamp, and it looks almost like the English word. Lampe is feminine, so it takes "la".
questions.meaning: light for a desk or room
questions.example: La lampe est sur la table.

questions.explanation: "le miroir" means mirror, the glass you look at yourself in. Miroir is masculine, so it takes "le".
questions.example: Le miroir est dans l'entrée.

questions.explanation: "la clé" means key, the thing that opens a door. Clé is feminine, so it takes "la".
questions.example: Où est la clé de la voiture ?

questions.explanation: "l'étagère" means shelf. Étagère is a feminine noun starting with a vowel, so la becomes l'.
questions.example: L'étagère est pleine de livres.

questions.explanation: "le tapis" is the piece of fabric laid on the floor, so it means "carpet" or rug. "le sol" is the floor itself.
questions.example: Le tapis est très doux.

questions.audioText: J'habite dans un petit appartement.
questions.explanation: "J'habite dans un petit appartement." means I live in a small apartment. The other choices change one word: garage, studio or grand (big).

questions.answer: La clé est sur la table.
questions.explanation: "La clé est sur la table." means The key is on the table. Clé is feminine, so it takes "la".

questions.prompt: Say that your kitchen is small.
acceptableAnswers: Ma cuisine est petite.
La cuisine est petite.
Ma cuisine est très petite.
Ma cuisine est minuscule.
Ma cuisine est toute petite.
Notre cuisine est petite.
Ma cuisine est exiguë.
Ma cuisine n'est pas grande.
questions.explanation: "Ma cuisine est petite." means My kitchen is small. Cuisine is feminine, so the adjective takes the feminine form petite.

units.title: Common Verbs (infinitives)
units.description: Everyday actions — High-frequency verbs in their infinitive form.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to eat" is…
questions.explanation: "manger" means to eat. It is a regular -er verb, as in Je mange une pomme.
questions.example: Nous mangeons à midi.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to drink" is… ___
questions.explanation: "boire" means "to drink", as in "boire de l'eau" (to drink water). It is an irregular verb, so learn it by heart.
questions.example: Je bois un verre d'eau.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to speak" is…
questions.explanation: "parler" means "to speak", as in "parler français". It is a regular -er verb.
questions.example: Elle parle très bien français.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to listen" is… ___
questions.explanation: "écouter" means "to listen", as in "écouter de la musique". Don't confuse it with "regarder", which means "to watch".
questions.example: J'écoute de la musique.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to read" is…
questions.explanation: "lire" means "to read", as in "lire un livre". "Regarder" means "to watch", not "to read".
questions.example: Je vais lire un livre.

questions.audioText: Je veux boire de l'eau.
questions.explanation: "Je veux boire de l'eau." means "I want to drink water"; listen for the verb boire (to drink) and the drink, de l'eau (water).

questions.prompt: Say that you want to drink water.
acceptableAnswers: Je veux boire de l'eau.
Je voudrais boire de l'eau.
J'aimerais boire de l'eau.
J'ai envie de boire de l'eau.
Je désire boire de l'eau.
questions.explanation: To say you want to do something, use vouloir followed by the infinitive, as in "Je veux boire de l'eau." "Je voudrais" (vouloir) and "J'aimerais" (aimer) are politer ways to say the same thing.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to write" is… ___
questions.explanation: "écrire" means "to write", as in "écrire une lettre". Don't mix it up with "lire", which means "to read".
questions.example: Elle écrit un message.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to sleep" is…
questions.explanation: "dormir" means "to sleep", as in "dormir huit heures". It is an irregular -ir verb.
questions.example: Nous dormons tard le dimanche.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to work" is… ___
questions.explanation: "travailler" means "to work", as in "travailler au bureau". It is a regular -er verb.
questions.example: Il travaille à Paris.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to study" is…
questions.explanation: "étudier" means "to study", as in "étudier le français". It looks like the English word "study".
questions.example: Elle étudie le français.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to play" is… ___
questions.explanation: "jouer" means "to play", as in "jouer au football". It is a regular -er verb.
questions.example: Les enfants jouent dehors.

questions.audioText: Je veux dormir ce soir.
questions.explanation: "Je veux dormir ce soir." means "I want to sleep tonight." The verb "dormir" (to sleep) sounds different from manger, partir and écrire.
"Je veux travailler au bureau." means "I want to work at the office." The verb "travailler" follows "je veux" in the infinitive.

questions.prompt: Say that you want to study French.
acceptableAnswers: Je veux étudier le français.
Je veux apprendre le français.
Je voudrais étudier le français.
Je voudrais apprendre le français.
J'aimerais étudier le français.
J'aimerais apprendre le français.
Je désire étudier le français.
J'ai envie d'étudier le français.
J'ai envie d'apprendre le français.
questions.explanation: "Je veux étudier le français." uses "vouloir" followed by the infinitive "étudier" (to study). "Je voudrais" is a politer way to say the same thing.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to walk" is… ___
questions.explanation: "marcher" means "to walk", as in "marcher dans le parc". It is a regular -er verb.
questions.example: Nous marchons dans le parc.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to run" is…
questions.explanation: "courir" means "to run", as in "courir dans le parc". It is an irregular -ir verb.
questions.example: Il court tous les matins.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to swim" is… ___
questions.explanation: "nager" means "to swim", as in "nager à la piscine". It is a regular -er verb.
questions.example: Elle nage très bien.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to cook" is…
questions.explanation: "cuisiner" means "to cook" (to prepare food); "jouer" is to play, "parler" to speak and "fermer" to close.
questions.example: Mon père cuisine ce soir.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to buy" is… ___
questions.explanation: "acheter" means to buy, as in acheter du pain (to buy bread).
questions.example: Je vais acheter du pain.

questions.audioText: J'aime nager à la piscine.
questions.explanation: "J'aime nager à la piscine." means "I like to swim at the pool"; listen for the start of the verb: nager (to swim) has no m sound, unlike manger (to eat).

questions.prompt: Say that you want to buy bread.
acceptableAnswers: Je veux acheter du pain.
Je voudrais acheter du pain.
J'aimerais acheter du pain.
J'ai envie d'acheter du pain.
Je désire acheter du pain.
Je souhaite acheter du pain.
questions.explanation: "Je veux acheter du pain." uses the infinitive acheter (to buy) after je veux (I want), and du pain for some bread.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to sell" is…
questions.explanation: "vendre" means to sell, the opposite of acheter (to buy). Don't confuse it with attendre, which means to wait.
questions.example: Il vend des fruits.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to open" is… ___
questions.explanation: "ouvrir" means to open, as in ouvrir la porte (to open the door).
questions.example: Elle ouvre la fenêtre.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to close" is…
questions.explanation: "fermer" means to close, the opposite of ouvrir (to open), as in fermer la fenêtre.
questions.example: Il ferme la porte.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to look" is… ___
questions.explanation: "regarder" means to look (at) or to watch, as in regarder la télé. It takes no word for at.
questions.example: Nous regardons un film.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to wait" is…
questions.explanation: "attendre" means "to wait" (for example, attendre le bus); "vendre" only looks similar and means to sell.
questions.example: Il faut attendre le bus.

questions.audioText: Je veux ouvrir la porte.
questions.explanation: "Je veux ouvrir la porte." means "I want to open the door." Listen for ouvrir (open) and porte (door); the other choices change one word: fermer (close), peindre (paint) or fenêtre (window).
"Je veux regarder la télé." means 'I want to watch TV.' Regarder takes no extra word for 'at' or 'to'.

questions.prompt: Say that you are waiting for the bus.
acceptableAnswers: J'attends le bus.
J'attends le bus ici.
Moi, j'attends le bus.
Je suis en train d'attendre le bus.
J'attends l'autobus.
Moi, j'attends l'autobus.
J'attends le car.
questions.explanation: "J'attends le bus." uses attendre (to wait), which needs no word for 'for' in French.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to help" is…
questions.explanation: "aider" means "to help"; it is a regular -er verb, as in « Je peux t'aider ? ».
questions.example: Je veux aider mon ami.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to love" is… ___
questions.explanation: "aimer" means "to love", and also "to like" for things, as in « J'aime le chocolat ».
questions.example: Tu vas aimer ce film.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to want" is…
questions.explanation: "vouloir" means "to want" (je veux un café); "avoir besoin de" is different and means to need.
questions.example: Nous voulons du thé.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to need" is… ___
questions.explanation: "avoir besoin de" means "to need" (j'ai besoin d'aide); "avoir envie de" means to feel like, "avoir peur de" to be afraid of and "avoir faim" to be hungry.
questions.example: Nous avons besoin de pain.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to live" is…
questions.explanation: "vivre" means "to live" (to be alive, or to live somewhere), as in « Je vis à Paris ».
questions.example: Ils vivent à Paris.

questions.audioText: Je veux aider mon ami.
questions.explanation: The sentence is "Je veux aider mon ami." and means "I want to help my friend"; the other choices change the verb to call, listen to or invite.

questions.prompt: Say that you want to help your friend.
acceptableAnswers: Je veux aider mon ami.
Je veux aider mon amie.
Je veux aider mon copain.
Je veux aider ma copine.
Je voudrais aider mon ami.
Je voudrais aider mon amie.
J'aimerais aider mon ami.
questions.explanation: "Je veux aider mon ami." uses "vouloir" (je veux) followed by the infinitive "aider"; the friend can be mon ami, mon amie or mon copain.

units.title: Animals
units.description: Common animals — Everyday animals, pets and wildlife.

questions.explanation: "le chien" means "dog"; it is masculine, so it takes "le".
questions.example: Le chien dort sur le canapé.

questions.explanation: "le chat" means "cat"; it is masculine, and the final -t is silent.
questions.example: Le chat est sur la table.

questions.explanation: "l'oiseau" means "bird"; "le" becomes "l'" before a vowel, and the word is masculine.
questions.example: L'oiseau chante dans l'arbre.

questions.explanation: "le cheval" means "horse"; it is masculine, and the plural is irregular: "les chevaux".
questions.example: Le cheval mange de l'herbe.

questions.explanation: "la vache" means "cow"; it is feminine, so it takes "la".
questions.example: La vache donne du lait.

questions.audioText: Le chat dort sur le lit.
choices: Le chat dort sur la table.
Le chien dort sur le lit.
Le chat dort sur le lit.
Le chat mange sur le lit.
questions.answer: Le chat dort sur le lit.
questions.explanation: The sentence "Le chat dort sur le lit." means the cat is sleeping on the bed; the other choices change the animal, the verb or the place.

questions.answer: J'ai un chien et un chat
questions.explanation: "J'ai un chien et un chat" means "I have a dog and a cat"; use "un" before masculine animal words like "chien" and "chat".

questions.prompt: Say that the horse is big.
acceptableAnswers: Le cheval est grand.
Le cheval est gros.
Le cheval est énorme.
Le cheval est très grand.
Le cheval est immense.
Le cheval est de grande taille.
questions.explanation: "Le cheval est grand." uses "le" because "cheval" is masculine, and "est grand" means "is big"; "gros" also works and suggests a large, heavy animal.
"le cochon" means "pig"; it is masculine, so it takes "le".
questions.example: Le cochon est rose.

questions.explanation: "le mouton" means "sheep"; it is masculine, so it takes "le".
questions.example: Le mouton est dans le champ.

questions.explanation: "la poule" is the live hen (feminine); chicken as meat is "le poulet".
questions.example: La poule a pondu un œuf.

questions.explanation: "le canard" means "duck"; it is masculine, and the final -d is silent.
questions.example: Le canard nage dans le lac.

questions.explanation: A rabbit is "le lapin" in French. Lapin is a masculine noun, so it takes le; le renard is a fox.
questions.example: Le lapin mange une carotte.

questions.audioText: Le canard est dans la rivière.
choices: Le lapin est dans la rivière.
Le cochon est dans la rivière.
Le canard est dans la rivière.
Le canard est dans la maison.
questions.answer: Le canard est dans la rivière.
questions.explanation: The sentence heard was "Le canard est dans la rivière." It says the duck is in the river; the other choices change one word to a different animal or place.

questions.prompt: Say that you have a rabbit.
acceptableAnswers: J'ai un lapin.
Je possède un lapin.
J'ai un lapin comme animal de compagnie.
J'ai un lapin domestique.
questions.explanation: "J'ai un lapin." uses j'ai (I have) with un, because lapin is a masculine noun.
A mouse is "la souris" in French. Souris is a feminine noun, so it takes la, unlike most animals in this list.
questions.example: La souris est sous la table.

questions.explanation: A fish is "le poisson" in French. Poisson is masculine and is spelled with a double s, which gives the s sound.
questions.example: Le poisson nage dans l'eau.

questions.explanation: A lion is "le lion" in French. The spelling is the same as in English, but the word is masculine and ends in a nasal vowel: the n is not pronounced as a separate sound.
questions.meaning: big wild cat with a mane
questions.example: Le lion dort au soleil.

questions.explanation: A tiger is "le tigre" in French. Note the -re ending, where English has -er, and the masculine article le.
questions.example: Le tigre est très grand.

questions.explanation: A bear is "l'ours" in French. Ours starts with a vowel, so le shortens to l'.
questions.example: L'ours dort en hiver.

questions.audioText: Le chat mange du poisson.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "Le chat mange du poisson.", meaning the cat eats fish. The other choices change the animal or the food to words that sound clearly different.
"Le lapin et la souris" means the rabbit and the mouse. Remember that souris is feminine, so it takes la.

questions.prompt: Say that you see a bear.
acceptableAnswers: Je vois un ours.
Je vois l'ours.
J'aperçois un ours.
Je vois un grand ours.
Moi, je vois un ours.
questions.explanation: "Je vois un ours." means I see a bear: je vois is "I see", and ours is masculine, so it takes un.
An elephant is "l'éléphant" in French. Éléphant starts with a vowel, so le shortens to l'. Note the two accents.
questions.example: L'éléphant est très gros.

questions.explanation: A monkey is "le singe" in French. Singe is a masculine noun, so it takes le.
questions.example: Le singe mange une banane.

questions.explanation: A wolf is "le loup" in French. The final p is silent, and l'ours is a bear.
questions.example: Le loup habite dans la forêt.

questions.explanation: A fox is "le renard" in French. Renard is a masculine noun, and its final d is silent.
questions.example: Le renard est rapide.

questions.explanation: A frog is "la grenouille" in French. Grenouille is a feminine noun, so it takes la, and le canard is a duck.
questions.example: La grenouille saute dans l'eau.

questions.audioText: Le loup mange le canard.
questions.explanation: You hear "Le loup mange le canard." It means the wolf eats the duck. To tell it from the other choices, listen for the animals (loup, canard) and for the verb mange (eats).

questions.prompt: Say that the fox is a wild animal.
acceptableAnswers: Le renard est un animal sauvage.
C'est un animal sauvage, le renard.
Le renard, c'est un animal sauvage.
questions.explanation: "Le renard est un animal sauvage." puts the adjective "sauvage" after the noun "animal", as most French adjectives go.
A snake is "le serpent" in French. Serpent is a masculine noun, and its final t is silent.
questions.example: Le serpent est long.

questions.explanation: "Turtle" is "la tortue". It is a feminine noun, so it takes "la" (une tortue).
questions.example: La tortue est très lente.

questions.explanation: "Bee" is "l'abeille". It is feminine (une abeille), and "la" shortens to "l'" before the vowel.
questions.example: L'abeille fait du miel.

questions.explanation: "Butterfly" is "le papillon". It is a masculine noun, so it takes "le" (un papillon).
questions.example: Le papillon est sur la fleur.

questions.explanation: "Spider" is "l'araignée". It is feminine (une araignée), and "la" becomes "l'" before the vowel.
questions.example: L'araignée est dans la salle de bain.

questions.audioText: Le serpent est dans le jardin.
choices: Le papillon est dans le jardin.
Le serpent est dans le jardin.
Le serpent est dans le lit.
La tortue est dans le jardin.
questions.answer: Le serpent est dans le jardin.
questions.explanation: "Le serpent est dans le jardin." means "The snake is in the garden." Listen for "serpent" (snake) and "jardin" (garden); the other choices swap in a different animal or place, such as "papillon" (butterfly), "tortue" (turtle) or "lit" (bed).

questions.answer: J'ai une tortue et un papillon
questions.explanation: "J'ai une tortue et un papillon" means I have a turtle and a butterfly. Tortue is feminine so it takes une, and papillon is masculine so it takes un.

questions.prompt: Say that the spider is big.
acceptableAnswers: L'araignée est grande.
Elle est grande, l'araignée.
L'araignée est très grande.
L'araignée est énorme.
L'araignée est grosse.
L'araignée est vraiment grande.
L'araignée est très grosse.
questions.explanation: "L'araignée est grande." uses the feminine adjective grande because araignée is a feminine noun.

units.title: Professions & Jobs
units.description: Talking about work — Common jobs and professions.

questions.explanation: "Doctor" is "le médecin", the usual word for the profession. You say "docteur" mainly when you address a doctor directly.
questions.example: Le médecin travaille à l'hôpital.

questions.explanation: "Nurse" is "l'infirmier" for a man and "l'infirmière" for a woman. "Le" becomes "l'" before the vowel.
questions.example: L'infirmier aide les malades.

questions.explanation: "Teacher" as a profession is "le professeur", used for secondary school and university teachers. In casual speech people often shorten it to "le prof".
questions.example: Le professeur aime son travail.

questions.explanation: "Engineer" is "l'ingénieur". It is masculine, and "le" becomes "l'" before the vowel.
questions.example: L'ingénieur travaille dans une usine.

questions.explanation: "Lawyer" is "l'avocat". Watch out: the same word also means "avocado".
questions.example: L'avocat parle au juge.

questions.audioText: Mon frère est médecin à Paris.
choices: Mon père est médecin à Paris.
Mon frère est avocat à Paris.
Mon frère est dentiste à Paris.
Mon frère est médecin à Paris.
questions.answer: Mon frère est médecin à Paris.
questions.explanation: The sentence "Mon frère est médecin à Paris." means 'My brother is a doctor in Paris.' Listen for the profession word "médecin", which differs clearly from "dentiste" or "avocat".

questions.prompt: Say that your sister is a nurse.
acceptableAnswers: Ma sœur est infirmière.
Ma sœur est une infirmière.
Ma sœur, elle est infirmière.
Ma sœur travaille comme infirmière.
Ma sœur est infirmière de métier.
Ma sœur exerce le métier d'infirmière.
questions.explanation: "Ma sœur est infirmière." uses the profession without an article after être, and a woman is "infirmière" with the feminine ending.

questions.prompt: The French word for "police officer" is…
questions.explanation: "Police officer" is "le policier". A female officer is "la policière".
questions.example: Le policier aide les gens.

questions.explanation: "Firefighter" is "le pompier". It comes from "pompe" (pump), and firefighters work in "la caserne des pompiers" (the fire station).
questions.example: Le pompier arrive vite.

questions.prompt: The French word for "cook" (the job) is…
questions.explanation: "le cuisinier" is the person who cooks as a job (a woman is la cuisinière); it comes from the verb cuisiner, to cook.
questions.example: Le cuisinier prépare le repas.

questions.explanation: "Waiter" is "le serveur", from the verb "servir" (to serve). A waitress is "la serveuse".
questions.example: Le serveur apporte le café.

questions.explanation: "l'agriculteur" is the person who works the land and raises crops or animals; the article elides to l' because the noun starts with a vowel.
questions.example: L'agriculteur travaille dans les champs.

questions.audioText: Le coiffeur travaille dans un salon.
choices: Le coiffeur travaille dans un hôpital.
Le pompier travaille dans un salon.
Le coiffeur travaille dans un salon.
Le coiffeur travaille dans un restaurant.
questions.answer: Le coiffeur travaille dans un salon.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "Le coiffeur travaille dans un salon." The other choices change the job or the workplace to a different word.

questions.answer: Je suis professeur dans une école
questions.explanation: "Je suis professeur dans une école" means "I am a teacher in a school". In French you say your job without an article after "je suis".

questions.prompt: Say that your brother is a cook.
acceptableAnswers: Mon frère est cuisinier.
Mon frère est un cuisinier.
Mon frère travaille comme cuisinier.
Mon frère, il est cuisinier.
Mon frère est cuisinier de métier.
Mon frère exerce le métier de cuisinier.
questions.explanation: "Mon frère est cuisinier." uses "être" plus the job without an article, which is the usual way to say what someone does.
"le chauffeur" is a driver as a job, such as a taxi or bus driver (un chauffeur de taxi).
questions.example: Le chauffeur attend devant l'hôtel.

questions.explanation: "le pilote" is the person who flies a plane; the word looks almost the same as the English "pilot".
questions.example: Le pilote est dans l'avion.

questions.explanation: artist → l'artiste. Common jobs and professions.
questions.example: L'artiste peint un tableau.

questions.explanation: "le musicien" means "musician", a person who plays music; a woman is la musicienne.
questions.example: Le musicien joue du piano.

questions.explanation: "l'écrivain" means "writer", a person who writes books; "le" becomes "l'" before the vowel "é".
questions.example: L'écrivain écrit un livre.

questions.audioText: Mon père est chauffeur de taxi.
choices: Mon oncle est chauffeur de taxi.
Mon frère est chauffeur de taxi.
Mon père est chauffeur de taxi.
Mon père est chauffeur de bus.
questions.answer: Mon père est chauffeur de taxi.
questions.explanation: You hear "Mon père est chauffeur de taxi.", meaning 'My father is a taxi driver'. Listen for "père" (not frère or oncle) and "taxi" (not bus).

questions.prompt: Say that your brother is a musician.
acceptableAnswers: Mon frère est musicien.
Mon frère est un musicien.
Mon frère, il est musicien.
Mon frère travaille comme musicien.
Mon frère est musicien de métier.
Mon frère exerce le métier de musicien.
questions.explanation: "Mon frère est musicien." uses the job directly after est without an article, which is the usual way to state someone's profession.
"le scientifique" means "scientist"; the word is the same for a man or a woman (la scientifique).
questions.example: Le scientifique travaille au laboratoire.

questions.explanation: "le dentiste" means "dentist", the person who looks after your teeth (les dents); a woman is la dentiste.
questions.example: Le dentiste regarde mes dents.

questions.explanation: "le comptable" is the person who keeps a company's accounts (un compte = an account); a woman is "la comptable".
questions.example: Le comptable travaille avec l'argent.

questions.explanation: "l'électricien" means electrician; "le" becomes "l'" because the word starts with a vowel.
questions.example: L'électricien répare la lampe.

questions.explanation: "le plombier" is the person who fixes pipes and taps; it comes from "plomb" (lead), the metal old pipes were made of.
questions.example: Le plombier répare la douche.

questions.audioText: Mon père est dentiste.
questions.explanation: The sentence is "Mon père est dentiste." and it means "My father is a dentist." The other jobs sound clearly different.
"Je suis plombier" means "I am a plumber." In French you say a job without "un" after "je suis".

questions.prompt: Say that your mother is an accountant.
acceptableAnswers: Ma mère est comptable.
Ma maman est comptable.
Ma mère est une comptable.
Ma mère travaille comme comptable.
Ma mère, elle est comptable.
Ma mère est comptable de métier.
Ma mère exerce le métier de comptable.
questions.explanation: "Ma mère est comptable." means "My mother is an accountant." After "est" the job needs no "un" or "une".
"le coiffeur" is the person who cuts your hair (la coiffure = hairstyle); a woman is "la coiffeuse".
questions.example: Le coiffeur coupe les cheveux.

questions.explanation: "le journaliste" means journalist; the word is the same for a woman, only the article changes: "la journaliste".
questions.example: Le journaliste écrit un article.

questions.explanation: "l'architecte" means architect; "le" becomes "l'" before a vowel, and the word is the same for a man or a woman.
questions.example: L'architecte dessine une maison.

questions.explanation: "le soldat" is a member of the army; it is a masculine noun and looks close to the English word soldier.
questions.example: Le soldat porte un uniforme.

questions.explanation: "le secrétaire" means secretary; for a woman you say "la secrétaire", and the spelling stays the same.
questions.meaning: office assistant who handles mail and calls
questions.example: Le secrétaire répond au téléphone.

questions.audioText: Mon père est coiffeur à Paris.
choices: Mon père est médecin à Paris.
Mon frère est coiffeur à Paris.
Mon père est coiffeur à Nice.
Mon père est coiffeur à Paris.
questions.answer: Mon père est coiffeur à Paris.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "Mon père est coiffeur à Paris.", meaning my father is a hairdresser in Paris; the other choices change the job, the person or the city.

questions.prompt: Say that your sister is a journalist.
acceptableAnswers: Ma sœur est journaliste.
Ma sœur travaille comme journaliste.
Ma sœur est une journaliste.
Ma sœur, elle est journaliste.
Ma sœur est journaliste de métier.
Ma sœur exerce le métier de journaliste.
questions.explanation: "Ma sœur est journaliste." is the simplest way to say it; after être, French usually drops the article before a profession and the word journaliste stays the same for a woman.

units.title: Question Words
units.description: Asking questions in French — Core question words and phrases.

questions.explanation: "qui" asks about a person (who); quel asks which, and quand asks when.
questions.example: Qui est ton professeur ?

questions.explanation: "quoi" means what at the end of a question or after a preposition, as in "Tu fais quoi ?" or "De quoi tu parles ?"; at the start of a question French uses "que" or "qu'est-ce que".
questions.example: Tu fais quoi ce soir ?

questions.explanation: "où" asks about a place (where); the grave accent separates it from ou, which means or.
questions.example: Où habites-tu ?

questions.explanation: "quand" asks about time (when); où asks where, and combien asks how much or how many.
questions.example: Quand est ton anniversaire ?

questions.explanation: "pourquoi" asks for a reason (why); the answer often starts with parce que (because).
questions.example: Pourquoi tu pleures ?

questions.audioText: Comment vous vous appelez ?
questions.explanation: "Comment vous vous appelez ?" asks what someone's name is, using comment, which means how. The other choices swap in pourquoi (why), quand (when) or où (where).
"Pourquoi tu pars maintenant ?" uses pourquoi (why) to ask for a reason, in the everyday spoken style where the word order stays the same.

questions.prompt: Ask a stranger politely when the train leaves.
acceptableAnswers: Quand part le train, s'il vous plaît ?
Le train part quand, s'il vous plaît ?
Quand est-ce que le train part, s'il vous plaît ?
À quelle heure part le train, s'il vous plaît ?
